mechanism_narrative: A sustained week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility indicates a gradual return to office-based work, which directly drives increased incidental retail and recreation visits during weekdays, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week rebound in TRANSIT usage, as observed in the latest data, signals increased public movement and willingness to engage in out-of-home activities, which will boost retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises by more than 3 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC declines over the subsequent 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent trend of decreasing time spent at home (RESIDENTIAL) and increasing time at workplaces (WORKPLACES) indicates a broader shift in daily routines towards out-of-home activities, which will collectively drive higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days, even if WORKPLACES increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases concurrently.

candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC falls in the subsequent 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent week-on-week decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates that people are spending less time at home, signifying a general increase in out-of-home activity and willingness to engage with the urban environment, which will lead to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, falling below a baseline threshold, suggests that essential trip frequency is decreasing, potentially freeing up time and shifting consumer focus towards discretionary spending and leisure, thereby increasing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 1.5% change from baseline
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 1.5% change from baseline, but RETAIL_REC declines over the subsequent 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in both TRANSIT usage and WORKPLACES attendance signifies a robust return to pre-pandemic commuting patterns and daily routines, creating more opportunities for retail and recreation engagement, which will drive higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing sustained increases.

mechanism_narrative: After a period of negative RETAIL_REC, the observed week-on-week increase indicates a stabilization and potential self-correction in consumer behavior, suggesting a likely upward trend in discretionary mobility over the immediate week, provided no new restrictions are introduced.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC shows a week-on-week increase after being negative for at least 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls in the subsequent 7 days, despite showing a week-on-week increase after a negative period.
